decision: mapped the Python plugin in three parts (pipeline, Comic Vine data layer, UI and config) before planning
why: a 12.3k-line port needs a shared map that every later worker reads

decision: proved the original Python modules run in-process under ComicRack's IronPython 2.7.4 from C#
why: this lets tests compare the port with the original code itself instead of a hand-written guess

decision: made one live Comic Vine call and one with a bad key
why: the API may have changed since March 2024
evidence: search HTTP 200 status_code 1, 3391 results; bad key HTTP 401 with status_code 100 in the body; key absent from both saved bodies

decision: set rigor high and wrote the plan with a done predicate
why: the plugin writes metadata into users' libraries in bulk and takes over existing settings

decision: kept the Apache 2.0 licence with a NOTICE crediting Cory Banack, and raised the GPL v2 linking question for the maintainer
why: a C# plugin compiles against ComicRack's GPL v2 assemblies; the licence call is not mine to make

decision: started two independent design sketches (Opus and Fable) for the project layout, core types, engine and UI boundary, threading, and ComicRack boundary
why: these choices shape every later file and are expensive to reverse, so compare two whole designs before building

decision: kept the Apache 2.0 licence
why: the maintainer decided this after being told that ComicRackCE is GPL v2

decision: changed the policy from keeping Python quirks to fixing the original's bugs, and listed the 10 bugs found so far plus 5 items still to classify
why: the maintainer asked for the bugs to be fixed, not ported

decision: received both design sketches; they agree on blocking command, Core assembly without WinForms or ComicRack, per-book state machine, typed field set, pure plan then one-step apply, typed ids, closed dialog choices
why: two independent models converging on the same structure is strong evidence it is right

decision: decided to settle live-window (nested loop) versus disabled-window (modal) by a prototype in ComicRack, not on paper
why: the behaviour (undo group, editor copy, second scrape, app close mid-run) can be observed directly
evidence: fable architecture.md open risk; opus tradeoffs

decision: chose the Opus sketch as the base: the scrape runs inside a modal ComicForm, and ComicRack's main window is disabled during a scrape
why: the Sonnet judge and my own reading agree on data safety: with a usable main window, an edit or a second scrape can race the merge, and the Fable sketch planned from a stale snapshot

decision: grafted the StepEntered trace and the sketch reading order from Fable, and wired CoverPreferences into ScrapeServices; the judge's other two grafts were already in the Opus sketch
why: checked the judge's claims against the sketch files instead of trusting them

decision: ruled on the 8 open behaviour questions: release date as blank is bug 11, five items kept as intended, URL encoding closed as not observable, rate limit ends the run
why: the maintainer asked for bugs to be fixed; deciding now keeps the workers unblocked

decision: built the solution with VS MSBuild and ComicRackDir (from COMICRACK_DIR), and made Build.ps1 fail when a test exe finds zero tests
why: dotnet build cannot build WinForms resx here, and a suite that silently runs nothing proves nothing

decision: ported IronPython's str(float), float(), and int() from the decompiled IronPython.dll instead of CPython's algorithms
why: the oracle is IronPython 2.7.4, and it differs from CPython (str(999999999999.5) is 1000000000000.0; int('- 5') is -5)
evidence: scratch ipy-decomp/StringFormatter.cs, LiteralParser.cs; oracle test Format_matches_str_of_float

decision: checked DatFile against persist_map and load_map in both directions, byte for byte after the header, and on seeded random lines; mutated PyStr twice to prove the oracle tests go red with the expected diff
why: a green differential test only counts if it can see a difference

decision: recorded two DatFile divergences: the header time is invariant HH:mm:ss, and whole numbers beyond 64 bits stay text
why: neither changes what any reader sees for keys the plugin writes

decision: did not launch ComicRack for the in-app proof, and left the probe and its run script in scratch
why: the user's ComicRack.exe was running, and the single-instance name ComicRackSingleInstance ignores -ac, so a launch would hand the arguments to the user's instance

decision: gave the port its own package name (Comic Vine Scraper .NET) and command key (comic-vine-scraper-net), sharing the Python settings folder
why: the same name installs into the Python plugin folder, where the old .py files keep loading and ComicRack keeps only one command per key; side by side install is also needed for the end-to-end comparison
evidence: ComicRack.Engine/PackageManager.cs CommitInstallPackage; PluginEngine dedupe by Key; cvs-phase2-task.md step 2

decision: handed Phase 2 (solution, build, packaging, Python oracle, DatFile slice, plugin skeleton, ComicForm host prototype, in-app proof) to one Opus owner on branch phase2-scaffold
why: the pieces are coupled through the solution layout, so one owner works in order with a check after each step

decision: verified phase 2 myself: clean rebuild, 0 warnings, 53 fast and 9 oracle tests green on x64, 18 flat files in the .crplugin
why: checked the artifact instead of the owner's report

decision: in-app proof of the ComicForm host left BLOCKED; did not close the user's ComicRack
why: ComicRack is single-instance and the user's copy (pid 83452) was running

decision: Fable review found the translation loader never turned backslash-n into a newline (129 strings), plus a number-format edge case, a cancel re-entrancy risk, and 4 unrecorded divergences
why: independent review by a different model family before merge
result: 5 fixes sent to a fresh Sonnet agent

decision: a Sonnet agent fixed the 5 review findings with a failing test first; 2 premises were wrong (IronPython has the same number bug; MTP already failed zero-test runs) and it said so
why: fresh agent per fix round, findings as the brief

decision: found MSB3277 (DiagnosticSource 6 vs 8) was passing a build that claimed warnings are errors; pinned 8.0.1 and set MSBuildTreatWarningsAsErrors
why: TreatWarningsAsErrors covers only compiler warnings; proved the new gate turns MSB3277 into an error before re-adding the pin
evidence: Directory.Build.props; tests csproj; build log 'error MSB3277'

decision: merged phase 2 into main (fast-forward)
why: reviewed, fixed, and verified; only the in-app proof is outstanding and it needs the user's ComicRack closed
